  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    # Retry delivery to possibly-unavailable remote mailservers.
    retry_on Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, Socket::ResolutionError, wait: :polynomially_longer

    # Net::SMTPServerBusy is SMTP error code 4xx, a temporary error.
    # Common one we've seen is 452 4.3.1 Insufficient system storage.
    # Patiently retry.
    retry_on Net::SMTPServerBusy, wait: :polynomially_longer

    # SMTP error 50x.
    rescue_from Net::SMTPSyntaxError do |error|
      case error.message

class User::Export < Export
  BATCH_SIZE = 100

  def download_url(**options)
    Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.user_export_url(user, self, script_name: account.slug, **options)
  end

  def description
    "the cards you can see in #{account.name}"
  end

  private
    def populate_zip
      ZipFile.create_for(file, filename: filename) do |zip|
        export_accessible_cards(zip)
      end
    end

    def filename
      "fizzy-cards-#{user.id}-#{(created_at || Time.current).utc.strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}.zip"
    end

    def authorized_for?(accessor)
      accessor.present? && accessor == user
    end

    def export_accessible_cards(zip)
      accessible_cards_scope.in_batches(of: BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
        cards = batch.preload(
          :board,
          :column,
          :tags,
          :steps,
          :closure,
          :goldness,
          :not_now,
          { creator: :identity },
          { assignees: :identity },
          { image_attachment: :blob },
          { rich_text_description: { embeds_attachments: :blob } },
          { comments: [ { creator: :identity }, { rich_text_body: { embeds_attachments: :blob } } ] }
        ).to_a

        cards.sort_by(&:number).each do |card|
          export_card(zip, card)
        end
      end
    end

    def accessible_cards_scope
      user.accessible_cards.published
    end

    def export_card(zip, card)
      blob_paths = {}
      used_names = Set.new

      image_entry = if card.image.attached?
        export_blob(zip, card, card.image.blob, blob_paths, used_names)
      end

      description_attachments = card.attachments.map do |embed|
        export_blob(zip, card, embed.blob, blob_paths, used_names)
      end

      comments_payload = card.comments.sort_by { |c| [ c.created_at, c.id ] }.map do |comment|
        comment_attachments = comment.attachments.map do |embed|
          export_blob(zip, card, embed.blob, blob_paths, used_names)
        end

        {
          id: comment.id,
          body: comment.body.to_plain_text,
          body_html: comment.body.to_s,
          creator: serialize_person(comment.creator),
          created_at: comment.created_at.utc.iso8601,
          updated_at: comment.updated_at.utc.iso8601,
          attachments: comment_attachments
        }
      end

      all_attachments = ([ image_entry ].compact + description_attachments + comments_payload.flat_map { |c| c[:attachments] })
        .uniq { |entry| entry[:path] }

      card_json = {
        id: card.id,
        number: card.number,
        title: card.title,
        status: card.status,
        description: card.description.to_plain_text,
        description_html: card.description.to_s,
        board: {
          id: card.board.id,
          name: card.board.name
        },
        column: serialize_column(card.column),
        creator: serialize_person(card.creator),
        assignees: card.assignees.map { |assignee| serialize_person(assignee) },
        tags: card.tags.map(&:title).sort,
        steps: card.steps.map { |step| { id: step.id, content: step.content, completed: step.completed } },
        closed: card.closed?,
        closed_at: card.closed_at&.utc&.iso8601,
        postponed: card.postponed?,
        golden: card.golden?,
        due_on: card.due_on&.iso8601,
        created_at: card.created_at.utc.iso8601,
        updated_at: card.updated_at.utc.iso8601,
        last_active_at: card.last_active_at.utc.iso8601,
        image: image_entry&.dig(:path),
        attachments: all_attachments,
        comments: comments_payload
      }

      zip.add_file("#{card.number}.json", JSON.pretty_generate(card_json))
    end

    def export_blob(zip, card, blob, blob_paths, used_names)
      path = blob_paths[blob.id]

      unless path
        safe_name = uniquify_filename(sanitize_filename(blob.filename.to_s), used_names)
        path = "#{card.number}/#{safe_name}"
        zip.add_file(path, compress: false) do |sink|
          blob.download { |chunk| sink.write(chunk) }
        end
        blob_paths[blob.id] = path
      end

      {
        filename: blob.filename.to_s,
        path: path,
        content_type: blob.content_type,
        byte_size: blob.byte_size
      }
    end

    def sanitize_filename(raw_name)
      cleaned = File.basename(raw_name.to_s).gsub(/[\/\\:\x00]/, "_").presence
      cleaned || "attachment"
    end

    def uniquify_filename(filename, used_names)
      return filename if used_names.add?(filename)

      ext = File.extname(filename)
      base = File.basename(filename, ext)
      counter = 1

      loop do
        candidate = "#{base} (#{counter})#{ext}"
        return candidate if used_names.add?(candidate)
        counter += 1
      end
    end

    def serialize_column(column)
      if column
        {
          id: column.id,
          name: column.name,
          color: column.color.to_s
        }
      end
    end

    def serialize_person(person)
      if person
        {
          id: person.id,
          name: person.name,
          email_address: person.identity&.email_address
        }
      end
    end
end

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/account/import.rb
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  STALE_THRESHOLD = 7.days

  belongs_to :identity
  belongs_to :account, optional: true

  has_one_attached :file, dependent: :purge_later

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  validate :ensure_file_attached, on: :create

  scope :stale, -> { where(status: %w[ completed failed ], updated_at: ...STALE_THRESHOLD.ago) }

  class << self
    def cleanup
      stale.find_each(&:destroy)
    end
  end

  def process_later
    Account::Import::ProcessJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def process_now
    processing!
    uploaded_keys = []

    ZipFile.read_from(file) do |zip|
      ApplicationRecord.transaction do
        imported_account = Account.create!(name: "Importing...")

        Current.with_account(imported_account) do
          id_map = Account::DataTransfer::IdMap.new(imported_account)
          manifest = Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(imported_account)

          manifest.each_record_set do |record_set|
            record_set.check(from: zip)
          end

          manifest.each_record_set do |record_set|
            record_set.import(from: zip, id_map: id_map, uploaded_keys: uploaded_keys)
          end

          ensure_system_user(imported_account)
          ensure_importer_access(imported_account)
          reindex_search(imported_account)
          reconcile_storage(imported_account)
        end

        update!(account: imported_account, status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current, failure_reason: nil)
      end
    end

    file.purge_later
    Current.without_account do
      ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
    end
  rescue => error
    cleanup_uploaded_files(uploaded_keys)
    file.purge if file.attached?
    reason = failure_message_for(error)
    update!(account: nil, status: :failed, failure_reason: reason)
    Current.without_account do
      ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
    end
  end

  private
    def ensure_file_attached
      unless file.attached?
        errors.add(:file, "must be selected")
      end
    end

    def ensure_system_user(imported_account)
      unless imported_account.users.exists?(role: :system)
        imported_account.users.create!(role: :system, name: "System")
      end
    end

    def ensure_importer_access(imported_account)
      existing_user = imported_account.users.find_by(identity: identity)

      if existing_user
        attrs = { active: true, verified_at: existing_user.verified_at || Time.current }
        attrs[:role] = :owner if imported_account.users.owner.where.not(id: existing_user.id).none? && !existing_user.owner?
        existing_user.update_columns(attrs)
      else
        importer_name = identity.users.first&.name.presence || identity.email_address.split("@").first
        importer_user = imported_account.users.create!(
          identity: identity,
          name: importer_name,
          role: :owner,
          active: true,
          verified_at: Time.current
        )
        grant_board_access(imported_account, importer_user)
      end
    end

    def grant_board_access(imported_account, user)
      now = Time.current
      access_rows = imported_account.boards.ids.map do |board_id|
        {
          id: ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate,
          account_id: imported_account.id,
          board_id: board_id,
          user_id: user.id,
          involvement: "access_only",
          created_at: now,
          updated_at: now
        }
      end
      Access.insert_all(access_rows) if access_rows.any?
    end

    def reindex_search(imported_account)
      imported_account.cards.published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(&:reindex)
      Comment.where(account_id: imported_account.id)
        .joins(:card)
        .merge(Card.published)
        .includes(:rich_text_body, :card)
        .find_each(&:reindex)
    end

    def reconcile_storage(imported_account)
      imported_account.boards.find_each(&:reconcile_storage)
      imported_account.reconcile_storage
    end

    def cleanup_uploaded_files(uploaded_keys)
      service = ActiveStorage::Blob.service
      uploaded_keys.each do |key|
        service.delete(key)
      rescue => delete_error
        Rails.logger.warn("[Import] Failed to clean up blob key #{key}: #{delete_error.message}")
      end
    end

    def failure_message_for(error)
      case error
      when Account::DataTransfer::InvalidExportError
        error.message
      when ZipFile::InvalidFileError
        error.message
      when JSON::ParserError
        "The archive contains corrupted JSON data."
      when ActiveStorage::IntegrityError
        "A file in the archive failed checksum verification and may be corrupted."
      else
        "The import could not be completed: #{error.message}"
      end
    end
end
EOF

steps.reasoning_content:
**Comprehensive Testing - Let's Dive In!**

Okay, time to get serious about these tests. We need to build a rock-solid system, so I'm thinking, let's cover every single requirement and edge case!

First, let's lay out the groundwork: we need to fully test those routes, covering everything in `test/routes_test.rb`. That's `/account/exports`, `/account/exports/:id`, `/account/imports/new`, `/account/imports`, `/account/imports/:id`, and then the user-specific stuff: `/users/:user_id/exports` and `/users/:user_id/exports/:id`.

Next, the model tests. `test/models/export_test.rb` is critical, especially when dealing with both `Account::Export` and `User::Export`. For `Account::Export`, we need to confirm it's building that `.zip` correctly – all the `Account::DataTransfer::Manifest` record sets, but *absolutely* excluding those internal `Export` attachments. Crucially, this needs to work flawlessly with both local disk storage *and* simulated S3 storage. We need to make sure the S3 service is correctly simulated with `upload_stream` and `download_chunk`.

Then, `User::Export` is a beast. We need to guarantee it's exporting *only* accessible, published cards—those the user can see. That means, it needs to include cards on boards where the user has the correct access, while carefully excluding cards on private boards where they do not, excluding cards from other accounts, and ensuring that no `drafted` cards are included! Each card must contain all its associated data – comments, tags, steps, creator, assignees, board, column, timestamps, and crucially, all those images and attachments! We'll need to carefully verify that *every* single picture and file is included in the `.zip` and that the binary data exactly matches the original, even duplicate filenames! And, we must confirm expiration logic is airtight: `expired?` should be false for a day, then true after. Also, `accessible_to?` and `Export.cleanup` need to be rigorously tested to purge expired exports and their blobs.

`test/models/account/import_test.rb` is where things get interesting. I'm thinking, let's test a full round-trip import of a rich account. This includes everything: multiple boards, both private and public, with various publications, columns, active and deactivated users, user avatars with variants, tags, cards with different types of content, comments, custom filters, webhooks, events, notifications... the whole shebang. The goal: a brand-new account with its own unique `id` and external account id; we want to make sure the original account is *completely* untouched.

The tests must confirm that all the boards, columns, cards (with number preservation), comments, steps, tags, assignments, reactions, mentions, identities, avatars, card images, and embedded files are all present and readable in the new account! We want to simulate that SaaS-to-OSS transfer scenario. Full-text search should function in the new account. We'll also be verifying that the storage ledger (`account.bytes_used` and `board.bytes_used`) is accurate, reflecting the actual size of the imported attachments.

require "test_helper"

class Account::ExportsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @account = accounts("37s")
    @admin = users(:kevin)
    @owner = users(:jason)
    @member = users(:david)
  end

  test "admin sees export button on account settings and downloads full account zip via email link" do
    sign_in_as @admin

    get account_settings_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "form[action='#{account_exports_path}']"

    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear

    assert_difference -> { Account::Export.count }, +1 do
      perform_enqueued_jobs do
        post account_exports_path
      end
    end

    assert_redirected_to account_settings_path

    export = Account::Export.last
    assert export.completed?

    assert_equal 1, ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_equal [ @admin.identity.email_address ], mail.to

    download_path = account_export_path(export)
    assert_includes mail.body.encoded, download_path

    get download_path
    assert_response :redirect
    follow_redirect!
    assert_response :redirect
    follow_redirect!
    assert_response :success
    assert_equal "application/zip", response.media_type

    # Link stops working after a day
    blob_path = rails_blob_path(export.file, disposition: "attachment")
    travel(1.day + 1.minute) do
      get download_path
      assert_response :gone

      get blob_path
      assert_response :forbidden
    end
  end

  test "owner can also export the account" do
    sign_in_as @owner

    assert_difference -> { Account::Export.count }, +1 do
      post account_exports_path
    end
    assert_redirected_to account_settings_path
  end

  test "non-admin member cannot see export button or export the whole account" do
    sign_in_as @member

    get account_settings_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "form[action='#{account_exports_path}']", count: 0

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Export.count } do
      post account_exports_path
    end
    assert_response :forbidden

    admin_export = @account.exports.create!(user: @admin)
    admin_export.build_now

    get account_export_path(admin_export)
    assert_response :forbidden
  end
end
EOF

  def materialize_storage

      latest_entry_id = storage_entries.maximum(:id)

  def reconcile_storage
    cursor_before = storage_entries.maximum(:id)
    real_bytes = calculate_real_storage_bytes
    cursor_after = storage_entries.maximum(:id)

    else
      ledger_bytes = cursor_after ? storage_entries.where(id: ..cursor_after).sum(:delta) : 0

steps.message: Let's update `reconcile_storage` in `Account::Import` to materialize storage snapshots immediately, update `perform_enqueued_jobs` in `Account::ImportsControllerTest`, and run all 32 tests!
steps.reasoning_content:
**Debugging Storage Reconciliation and Job Execution**

Okay, let's break this down. First, I see an issue with `Storage::Totaled` and `Storage::Entry`. During the `board.reconcile_storage` process, it looks like `Storage::Entry` entries were being recorded with the correct `account_id`, `board_id`, and `delta`. The problem is that the `account.storage_entries` already gained all the `board_bytes` from `board.reconcile_storage`, which means that `account.reconcile_storage` was seeing a `diff == 0` when it ran.

Furthermore, `reconcile_storage` was only enqueuing `materialize_storage_later` as a `Storage::MaterializeJob` instead of running `materialize_storage` synchronously. That means that the accurate byte usage (`bytes_used_exact`) was present, while `bytes_used` (the materialized snapshot) remained at `0` until `materialize_storage` eventually ran.

The fix? It's clear that calling `board.materialize_storage` on each board AND `imported_account.materialize_storage` synchronously *inside* `reconcile_storage(imported_account)` will ensure that BOTH `bytes_used` AND `bytes_used_exact` are immediately accurate.

Now, let's move on to the second failure regarding the email delivery count. Why was `ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size` equal to `0` when `perform_enqueued_jobs` (without a block!) was called in `Account::ImportsControllerTest`?

The root of this is the behavior of Rails' `ActiveJob::TestHelper`.

I understand it now. `perform_enqueued_jobs` **WITH A BLOCK** (e.g., `perform_enqueued_jobs do ... end`) sets `perform_enqueued_jobs = true` recursively. That means jobs that were enqueued BY other jobs (like `MailDeliveryJob` enqueued by `Account::Import::ProcessJob`) also get run! steps.reasoning_content:
**Monotonic UUIDv7 Preservation: A Revelation!**

Wow, this is quite a discovery! Looking at `lib/rails_ext/active_record_uuid_type.rb`, I've realized something significant about `SecureRandom.uuid_v7`.  It's using a 48-bit millisecond timestamp plus some random bits (`rand_a`), unless you explicitly specify `extra_timestamp_bits: 12`.  This is particularly interesting in the context of `IdMap` and its monotonic UUIDv7 generation.

The core of it is this: when `SecureRandom.uuid_v7` is called multiple times within the same millisecond, the initial 48-bit timestamp is the *same*.  The following 12 bits are random. This means there's a 50/50 chance the subsequent UUID will be numerically *less* than the first, even within the same millisecond!  That's a real issue for ensuring strictly increasing UUIDs in a high-volume scenario like a bulk import.

But here's where it gets exciting. If we ensure `IdMap` generates monotonically increasing UUIDs (using `SecureRandom.uuid_v7(extra_timestamp_bits: 12)` and tracking `@last_generated_uuid`), we can solve this.  If a new candidate UUID is less than the last generated one, we can increment, regenerate, or, even better, *preserve the original `old_id`'s timestamp*.

The brilliance of UUIDv7 is in its structure: the first 48 bits are the timestamp, followed by version and sequence bits, and then the critical 62 random bits. So if we were to preserve the top 64 bits (timestamp + sequence) from a valid `old_id` and *only* randomize the bottom 62 bits, we're effectively guaranteeing temporal ordering!

Think about this:

1.  If `old_id_1` and `old_id_2` have different timestamps, even if they were generated out of order and if their timestamps are `T1` and `T2`, the new IDs generated by this system will preserve this ordering:  `T1 < T2` will always be `new_id_1 < new_id_2`.
2.  If the test had two steps created within the *same* millisecond and `step1.id > step2.id`, we've got an issue! However, the key here is to check *why* they were created. Checking lines 18-19 of `test/models/account/import_test.rb`, we see that the test creates two steps using `card.steps.create!`. Before export, `ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.generate` calls `SecureRandom.uuid_v7` *without* the `extra_timestamp_bits: 12`! This can cause `step2.id < step1.id` to be present in `@source_account` *before* the export! Because `export_records` sorts by `order(:id)`, this could have a scrambling effect.

By preserving the timestamp and sub-ms bits, we guarantee correct order across *all* accounts. Preserving the exact historical ordering of old IDs during the import process by keeping `old_id`'s top 64 bits ensures monotonic ordering of `order(:id)` during the import!

Now, let's investigate the  `app/models/card/multistep.rb` to understand how the `Card` orders its steps... This is crucial to see what order will be affected.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Cross-Database Export/Import Deep Dive**

Okay, so I've got this keyed SHA1 calculation with `OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.base64digest Marshal.dump(transformations)` – completely portable, which is great. Now, I need to thoroughly test this cross-database import/export, and specifically the edge cases, especially between SQLite and MySQL. Remember, this is about moving data between OSS and SaaS instances.

I'm thinking about ALL the data types and how they behave.

First, **UUIDs**: The `record.attributes` deserializes UUIDs into 25-char base36 strings. Then, I am making sure the `model.insert_all!` serializes them back to 16-byte binary. That will be the same on both SQLite and MySQL. Good.

Next, **JSON columns**: Both databases store and retrieve Ruby hashes, and `ActiveRecord::Type::Json#serialize` handles the conversion to and from JSON. That should be seamless.

Then, **serialized text columns**: Again, `JSON.generate` and `JSON.parse` round-trip Ruby `Array` or `Hash` objects, and `ActiveRecord::Type::Serialized` handles the serialization. Consistent.

For **Enums**: We're dealing with string enum names. `EnumType#serialize` is doing the work to ensure consistency. It's either an integer or string in both databases.

**Booleans**: `ActiveModel::Type::Boolean#serialize` ensures that `true` and `false` are consistently mapped to `1` and `0`. Perfect.

**Timestamps**: UTC ISO-8601 with microseconds is the format. `TimeZoneConverter#serialize` is the hero here, handling it correctly on both sides.

**Webhooks Safety**: Wait, before I move on - what about webhooks? When importing, I need to confirm that `insert_all!` skips those `Event` creation callbacks. Need to be sure those historical events don't fire during the import, spamming those URLs.

But there's one more subtle case. What if an `Identity` is created during an import, but the import later *fails*? For example, a new `Identity` is created inside a `UserRecordSet` transaction, but then `FileRecordSet` fails. I'm testing this scenario to confirm that because of the `ApplicationRecord.transaction`, the entire transaction should roll back, including the newly created `Identity`. The existence of the new identity should be false and the count completely unchanged.

Now that the data handling is secure, I'll go through the updates and tests: the UX refinements, portable HTML attachment paths for `User::Export`, friendly HTML for 404/410 errors in the exports directory, import link in the sessions menu, and some test cases.

Let's get this done. Let's make the changes and run the tests!

steps.message:
I have implemented data export and import for Fizzy:

### Summary of Changes

1. **Streaming ZIP Storage (`ZipFile`, `ZipFile::Writer`, `ZipFile::Reader`, `ZipFile::EntryIO`, `ZipFile::RemoteIO`)**:
   - Fixed `ZipFile::Writer` streaming byte-size and checksum tracking for S3 multipart uploads.
   - Added `ZipFile.read_from` with `ZipFile::Reader` (lazy central-directory parsing via `ZipKit::FileReader`), `ZipFile::EntryIO` (chunked streaming extraction), and `ZipFile::RemoteIO` (buffered HTTP/S3 chunked range reads via `download_chunk`) to handle very large archives on both local disk and S3 without loading archives into memory.

2. **Account & User Data Exports (`Export`, `Account::Export`, `User::Export`, `Export::BuildJob`, `ExportMailer`)**:
   - **Admin Account Export**: Admins and owners can export the entire account as a `.zip` from Account Settings (`POST /account/exports`, `GET /account/exports/:id`).
   - **User Profile Export**: Any signed-in user can export the published cards they have access to from their own profile page (`POST /users/:user_id/exports`, `GET /users/:user_id/exports/:id`). Each card is exported as JSON with its comments and metadata alongside every attached picture and file (card header images, description embeds, and comment embeds).
   - **Email & 1-Day Link Expiration**: `ExportMailer` sends an email with the download link when the background build finishes. Download links (and underlying ActiveStorage blob authorization) expire after 1 day (`24.hours`), returning `410 Gone`, and `Export.cleanup` is scheduled in `config/recurring.yml` to purge expired exports.

3. **Full Account Import (`Account::Import`, `Account::DataTransfer::*`, `Account::ImportsController`, `Account::Import::ProcessJob`, `ImportMailer`)**:
   - Signed-in users can upload an account `.zip` at `/account/imports/new` (`POST /account/imports`, `GET /account/imports/:id`), creating a new account with all boards, columns, entropies, publications, cards, comments, steps, tags, assignments, reactions, mentions, custom filters, webhooks, events, notifications, people/identities, ActionText rich texts (with portable GID rewriting across instances), and ActiveStorage files, followed by full-text search reindexing and storage ledger reconciliation.
   - Sends a completion email when finished, or a failure email with the specific failure reason if the archive is invalid, incomplete, or corrupted.
   - Wraps database imports in a transaction and cleans up any uploaded storage keys and the temporary `.zip` attachment on failure so an incomplete import leaves nothing behind.
